explainer.heading: Lakhs and crores
explainer.body: In the Indian system we group digits as 3, then 2, 2, 2 from the right: 1,00,000 is one lakh and 1,00,00,000 is one crore. 100 lakh make 1 crore.
explainer.example: A cricket stadium holds about 1,00,000 people, so one lakh is roughly a full stadium.
explainer.hook: Lakh has 5 zeros, crore has 7: L-5, C-7 (think 'Lucky 5, Champion 7').

explainer.heading: Millions and billions
explainer.body: The international system groups digits in threes: 1,000,000 is one million and 1,000,000,000 is one billion. 10 lakh = 1 million and 100 crore = 1 billion.
explainer.example: India's population is around 140 crore, which is about 1.4 billion.

explainer.heading: Estimating big numbers
explainer.body: Round large numbers to the nearest lakh, crore or thousand to compare or add them quickly, then check with exact numbers if needed.
explainer.example: A school with 1,987 students and another with 2,034 together have about 4,000 students.
explainer.hook: Round first, then calculate - big numbers become small.

explainer.heading: How big is a crore really?
explainer.body: Counting one number every second without stopping, one lakh takes over a day and one crore takes more than 115 days.
explainer.example: If you save ₹1 every day, reaching ₹1 lakh would take about 274 years!
explainer.hook: Crore = 100 times a lakh - a huge jump.

questions.why: 48,900 is less than 50,000, so it rounds down to 7,00,000.

questions.q: A city has 25 lakh people. How many millions is that?
About how long would it take to count to 1 lakh at one number per second?
questions.why: 1,00,000 seconds ≈ 27.8 hours, a little over a day.

questions.q: Explain why the Indian and international systems place commas differently, with an example.
questions.ans: Indian system groups 3 digits from the right then 2s (lakh, crore); international groups in 3s (thousand, million). Example: 1,00,000 vs 100,000.
questions.why: Different naming units: lakh/crore vs million/billion.

questions.q: A factory makes 2,50,000 pencils a month. How many pencils in a year? (digits only)
